newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Fantozzi says against touching severance.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Fantozzi says against touching severance.

text.p: Italian Foreign Trade minister Augusto Fantozzi said he was against touching severance pay in a planned mini-budget but could not rule out the government taking some action on it to help cut the country's deficit.

He said any levy on severance pay would be a "further hidden burden" for companies. "No-one is excluding the possibility that the measure might be included in the mini-budget but it is certainly not taken for granted," he told reporters.
Cesare Romiti, chairman of industrial giant Fiat, warned the government on Friday that it would face industrial opposition if severance pay was touched in the mini-budget.
Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi has indicated the package, due by the end of April, will raise around 14 trillion lire in a final bid to reduce the deficit to 3.0 percent of GDP.
One of the expected measures is to put a levy on employee severance payment funds which companies use as cash flow.
Labour Minister Tiziano Treu was quoted saying in the Italian press on Monday that a levy on the total amount of severance pay funds was unthinkable "but something can be done."
He said he wanted to avoid a "war" with industrialists. "But if an effort is demanded from all parties then companies must do their bit."
